title: Comparative Guide to BPM Tools for Brazilian Companies
summary: Comparative guide to BPM tools for Brazilian companies: evaluation criteria, integrations, and how to choose in 2026.
body_markdown:
BPM tools for Brazilian companies vary widely in automation, local integrations, and support quality. This guide brings together the criteria that actually matter when comparing options, without pointing to one single right answer for everyone.


Companies in Brazil face specific challenges: integrating with local ERPs like Omie and Conta Azul, teams that run much of their communication through WhatsApp, and the need to comply with national tax rules.


That's why comparing BPM tools on interface alone isn't enough. You need to look at objective criteria that affect day-to-day operations.


## Comparison criteria: automation


- Volume of native, no-code automations available
- Reliance on intermediaries like Zapier or Make
- Support for triggers by event, field, or button
- Execution logs for automations, for auditing
- Ability to handle multiple conditional stages


## Comparison criteria: integration and localization


- Native integration with ERPs used in Brazil, like Omie and Conta Azul
- Support for WhatsApp Business as an operational channel
- Availability of support and documentation in Portuguese
- Open API and webhooks to connect internal systems
- Compliance with Brazilian date and currency formats


## Comparison criteria: scalability and usage


- Ease of setting up workflows without relying on developers
- Support for multiple departments on the same platform
- Customization of fields, permissions, and views
- Security certifications, such as SOC 2
- Cost per user versus cost per module or process


Tools like Notion, Airtable, ClickUp, Pipefy, Monday, and Jestor come up in these searches. The right choice depends on the level of automation, integration, and process customization the company needs.

## Frequently asked questions


**How do I choose among so many BPM tools?** Compare native automations, local integrations, and how easy the tool is to use without code. See an example at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Do BPM tools require programming?** The most modern ones use visual, no-code setup, removing the need for developers for most workflows.


**Are BPM and ERP the same thing?** No. BPM organizes operational processes, while the ERP handles the company's fiscal and accounting side.


Evaluating BPM tools with clear criteria helps you avoid switching systems months into implementation.
